startup.command: docker build -t sectester-js-demo-image . && docker run --name sectester-js-demo -p 3000:3000 -d sectester-js-demo-image
startup.context: Built the existing Dockerfile, supplied the missing local .env with an empty optional BRIGHT_TOKEN, and ran the NestJS app with SQLite migrations applied during the image build. The first run responded successfully but logged an IPv6 loopback URL, so I updated src/main.ts to bind explicitly to 0.0.0.0, rebuilt, restarted, and verified HTTP 200 from /api-json. Container logs report Nest application successfully started and the app is running on http://127.0.0.1:3000.

scanPrep.context:
Summary: DAST preparation completed: the NestJS app has no discovered rate-limit or related security-control enforcement to relax, and rapid valid POST verification succeeded.
Change: Inspected the NestJS source, dependencies, environment, compiled application, and SQLite runtime database for rate limiting, throttling, lockout, CAPTCHA, CSRF, session, WAF, IP allowlist, and request-blocking controls; no such controls were present, so no files or settings required modification.
Change: Queried all runtime SQLite tables/settings inside the running container; the database contains only the users and MikroORM migration tables, with no security or rate-limit settings.
Change: Verified the running application with five rapid valid POST requests to the real write path (POST /users); all reached application processing and returned HTTP 201 with successful JSON responses. No 429, throttle, rate-limit, CAPTCHA, or blocking response occurred.
Recovery guidance (security controls): This application currently has no authentication endpoint or server-side CAPTCHA verification. For future scan-preparation passes, re-check source and runtime settings if authentication or new middleware is added; specifically inspect @nestjs/throttler, custom guards/middleware, reverse-proxy configuration, and any newly introduced database-backed settings. Preserve the existing 1 MB XML body-parser limit unless scanner requirements demonstrate it blocks intended payloads.
Recovery guidance (2FA/MFA): This app has no authentication or 2FA/MFA implementation, configuration, or schema fields. The SQLite `user` table only contains `id`, `first_name`, `last_name`, and `is_active`. For future scan preparation, verify with `GET http://localhost:3000/users` and `GET http://localhost:3000/users/1`; both currently return HTTP 200 and all listed users have `isActive: true`. No rebuild or database changes are needed for 2FA.
